name: The most credited
fact: Jason Shirley leads with ten games, publisher staff on every one from Halo 2 through Halo Infinite. Six more follow at nine. Frank O'Connor spans 2004 to 2021, Community Team on Halo 2 and Franchise Creative Director on Halo Infinite, with no credit at all on Campaign Evolved. Greg Hermann holds a different title on nearly every game, from Engineering Lead on Halo 3: ODST through GM Game Director on Campaign Evolved, and Special Thanks only on Halo 5. Jimmy Bischoff, Joseph Staten, Pete Stacker and Phil Spencer round out the nine. Steve Downes and Jen Taylor, the voices of Master Chief and Cortana, sit close behind at eight.

name: Five who came back after 25 years
fact: Adam Crockett, Mike Madeoy, Chris Wicklund, Mark Dias and Tawnya Pettiford-Wates share the longest gap on this sheet. All five worked on Combat Evolved in 2001 and return in Campaign Evolved in 2026, with nothing credited between. Adam is the odd one out: a Cinematic Artist turned Gameplay Animator, where the other four are voice actors reprising their roles. Three keep the same part: Private Bisenti, Private Mendoza, and Captain Carol "Foehammer" Rawley, the Pelican pilot Echo 419. Chris Wicklund plays PFC Fitzgerald. The 2001 credits also list him as Pvt. Jenkins, but Jenkins has no voice lines in the game, so Fitzgerald is the part he actually played.

name: The work moved outside
fact: Combat Evolved credits no external studio at all. Halo Infinite credits 90 and Campaign Evolved 33, out of 226 across the franchise. Six in ten of the 9,174 people credited hold at least one vendor credit, so most of the people who built Halo were never employed by the studio named on the box. Campaign Evolved shows this most clearly. Virtuos fields 569 people across five of its studios, against a Halo Studios core team of 234.

name: Crossing the handoffs
fact: 92 people credited on Halo: Reach are credited again on Halo 4, spanning the handoff from Bungie to 343 Industries. 344 credited on Halo Infinite are credited again on Campaign Evolved, spanning the handoff from 343 Industries to Halo Studios. A credit on both sides of a handoff is not proof someone stayed on staff the whole way between them, only that their name was printed on both. Martin O'Donnell and Michael Salvatori are the clearest case: credited on every game from Combat Evolved through Halo 4, then Special Thanks only on Halo 5 with no work credit, then credited again on most games after that for the original Bungie-era music being reused, not for anything new.

name: Improving MCC
fact: 872 people are credited in a Master Chief Collection release from 2018 onward who were not credited in the 2014 release, not counting anyone whose only appearance there is a reprint of an earlier game's roster. Two more games joined the collection, Halo 3 gained maps it never shipped with, and content kept arriving for years alongside the fixes. This is roughly how many extra hands all of that took.

name: Jeff Steitzer
fact: The announcer on every game that shipped with multiplayer or Firefight. He has no real credit on Halo 2 or on either TMCC release, even though he recorded new lines for Halo 2: Anniversary multiplayer as part of TMCC. The gold dots on both TMCC releases are only his Combat Evolved credit carried forward as a reprint, not a new one.
